chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I wash in the bathroom (latrine) in which I urinate, and upon me are Sindian slippers.' So he said: 'If the water that flows from your body hits the bottom of your feet, then do not wash your feet.'
ai.seo_question: Do I need to wash my feet if I am wearing slippers while washing in a bathroom?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the mechanics of ritual purity (*taharah*) by distinguishing between the necessity of washing the feet and the sufficiency of flowing water (*may al-jar*) in specific contexts. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that if water flows over a body part during the main washing process, it may suffice for purification even if the area is not explicitly scrubbed, provided the water reaches the required extent. The mention of 'Sindian slippers' reflects the material culture of the time and underscores the practical application of these rules in daily life.
